title: Undocumented Background Constructor Threads
pattern: A library constructor that spawns long-lived background threads without indicating this in its doc-comment or API behavior.
why_bad: Violates reader expectations. Callers expect the application to exit when `main` completes. If background threads are left active silently, the application hangs or behaves non-deterministically without any clear logging or documentation.
detection: Struct constructors spawning threads or registering async runtime loops, where the doc-comment lacks standard concurrency or lifecycle markers.
counterexample: A constructor doc-comment declaring lifecycle behavior: 'Spawns background network polling threads that keep the runtime active until `shutdown()` is called.'
fix: Document the threading model in the constructor's doc-comment, or restructure the API to require explicit spawn/run method calls.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 18.2 ("Nonobvious Code").
